sources.title: Pittayawat Pittayaporn, The Phonology of Proto-Tai
sources.note: Cornell dissertation checked for comparative reconstruction, daughter-language evidence, contact, reconstructed phonology, vocabulary, and the analytical status of Proto-Tai.

sources.title: Glottolog bibliography record for Pittayaporn 2009
sources.note: Max Planck bibliographic record checked for authorship, title, institution, year, and dissertation extent.

sources.title: Chulalongkorn University, Kra-Dai Languages bibliography
sources.note: University overview checked for family terminology, branches, modern distribution, diversity in southern China, and research cautions.

sources.title: The Tai-Kadai Languages
sources.note: Scholarly reference volume checked for family diversity, Tai subgroup descriptions, grammar, scripts, and distinctions among modern languages.

sources.title: The Languages and Linguistics of Mainland Southeast Asia
sources.note: Scholarly handbook checked for contact, convergence, multilingualism, and the danger of turning language-family labels into bounded peoples.

sources.title: Phylogenetic evidence reveals early Kra-Dai divergence and dispersal in the late Holocene
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open study checked for model-based divergence estimates, southern-China hypotheses, branch structure, archaeological comparison, and uncertainty.

sources.title: Contrasting modes of cultural evolution: Kra-Dai languages and weaving technologies
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for reconstructible weaving vocabulary, loom evidence, technology transfer, southern distribution, and explicit difficulty linking languages to archaeological cultures.

sources.title: Layers of Chinese Loanwords in Proto-Southwestern Tai
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical-linguistic study checked for later Proto-Southwestern Tai dispersal dating and evidence from stratified Chinese loans.

sources.title: The linguistic geography of southern China: language origins and dispersals
sources.note: Archived scholarly chapter checked for Kra-Dai diversity, riverine dispersal proposals, multilingual southern China, and geographic inference limits.

sources.title: Kra-Dai and the Proto-History of South China and Vietnam
sources.note: Journal article checked as one proposed synthesis connecting historical linguistics with south-China texts and geography; speculative identifications remain labeled as proposals.

sources.title: James Norquest, A Phonological Reconstruction of Proto-Hlai
sources.note: University dissertation checked to distinguish Hlai reconstruction from Proto-Tai and to show deeper Kra-Dai branch diversity.

sources.title: Roger Blench, Unearthing Southeast Asia’s Past: Daic prehistory
sources.note: Archaeolinguistic review checked for competing homeland proposals, reconstructed subsistence vocabulary, ethnographic analogy, and warnings about thin archaeology.

sources.title: Weera Ostapirat, Kra-Dai and Austronesian
sources.note: Historical-linguistic article checked for proposed sound correspondences and the debated higher-order Austro-Tai relationship.

sources.title: The Austronesian Homeland and Dispersal
sources.note: Annual Review article checked for Austronesian evidence and chronology used only to frame, not settle, proposed Kra-Dai relationships.

sources.title: Genomic Insights Into the Demographic History of the Southern Chinese
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review checked for admixture, multiple migrations, language-genetics mismatches, and limits on assigning ancestry to reconstructed languages.

sources.title: Reanalyzing the genetic history of Kra-Dai speakers from Thailand
sources.note: Peer-reviewed population-genetics study checked for present sampling, interaction, later dispersal models, and the prohibition on treating genes as languages.

sources.title: Tracking Proto-Porcelain in Bronze Age Lingnan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeology checked for kiln technology, production and consumption networks, and culturally mixed Bronze Age Lingnan material evidence.

sources.title: Archaeological Observations on the Development of Lingnan Culture
sources.note: University research database entry checked for archaeological periodization, pottery, Bronze Age development, and interpretive caution.

sources.title: The Archaeology of Asia-Pacific Navigation
sources.note: Open scholarly volume checked for Lingnan exchange, waterways, coastal interaction, imported forms, and changing material traditions.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Art of South and Southeast Asia
sources.note: Museum scholarly guide checked for limited prehistoric evidence, Ban Chiang and Dong Son chronology, bronze skill, ceramics, and modern-border cautions.

sources.title: British Museum, Dong Son Culture collection scope
sources.note: Museum collection authority checked for broad Dong Son date range and documented object types without assigning them to Proto-Tai speakers.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Year One
sources.note: Museum publication checked for Dong Son drum distribution, bronze casting, burial models, political meanings, and uncertain functions.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Model of a Bronze Drum
sources.note: Museum object record checked for a later Vietnamese drum model, chronology, tomb context, and interaction after the atlas interval.

sources.title: UNESCO, Ban Chiang Archaeological Site
sources.note: World Heritage documentation checked for regional prehistoric settlement, agriculture, ceramics, metals, burials, and the limits of modern national labels.

sources.title: Charles Higham, The Archaeology of Mainland Southeast Asia
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis checked for Bronze and Iron Age settlements, agriculture, exchange, social differentiation, and evidence gaps.

sources.title: Archaeological and genetic insights into the origins of domesticated rice
sources.note: PNAS review checked for rice domestication evidence, regional spread, and distinctions among crops, languages, genes, and archaeological sites.

sources.title: The domestication process and domestication rate in rice
sources.note: Science study checked for archaeobotanical sequences and why cultivated rice cannot by itself identify the language spoken by its growers.

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, King Ram Khamhaeng Inscription
sources.note: UNESCO record checked for the much later 1292 traditional dating and importance of early Thai script heritage.

sources.title: UNESCO nomination file, King Ram Khamhaeng Inscription
sources.note: Nomination file checked for the inscription’s discovery, study, authenticity debate, and documentary context.

sources.title: Unicode Standard, Tai Tham code chart
sources.note: Technical standard checked for later Tai Tham script names, characters, languages, and contemporary encoding; not used as ancient Proto-Tai writing.

sources.title: British Library, Alphabetum Syamense
sources.note: Collection record checked for a later seventeenth-century Thai syllabary, Thai and Latin scripts, paper, diplomatic context, and preservation.

sources.title: UNESCO case study, Natural Dyeing and Silk Weaving in Surin Province
sources.note: Living-heritage case checked for household and workshop labor, family teaching, dyes, ritual, markets, and clearly modern scope.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Thailand
sources.note: UNESCO inventory checked for living Thai heritage diversity, community transmission, education, food, performance, and recent safeguarding.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Nuad Thai
sources.note: Living-heritage record checked for a documented modern traditional-care practice, training, and community transmission; not backdated to Proto-Tai.

sources.title: WHO, The Kingdom of Thailand health system review
sources.note: Health-system review checked only for modern institutional change and access; it supplies no Iron Age medical evidence.

sources.title: UNICEF, Water, sanitation and hygiene
sources.note: Public-health source checked for why water, toilets, hygiene, maintenance, and child safety belong together; used only for modern framing.

sources.title: UNESCO, bringing living heritage to the classroom
sources.note: Education project checked for community bearers, teachers, children, safeguarding, and the difference between living transmission and prehistoric schooling.

sources.title: Archaeological Studies on Gender in Early East Asia
sources.note: Cambridge Element checked for methods, evidence bias, networks, and cautions against assigning fixed gender roles from sparse objects.

sources.title: Ancient Human Parasites in Ethnic Chinese Populations
sources.note: Peer-reviewed repository record checked for rare direct evidence from latrines, burials, and parasites and the small ancient Chinese sample.

sources.title: University of Cambridge, ancient latrine on the Silk Road
sources.note: Research report checked for a later, distant latrine, hygiene sticks, parasites, and the sort of direct evidence absent for the card’s proposed subject.

proposedOverrides.name: Proto-Tai reconstruction and possible communities
proposedOverrides.summary: Approximate 400 to 323 BCE atlas layer whose north-China geometry conflicts with Proto-Tai linguistic geography; treated as a reconstructed-language hypothesis, not a state, ethnicity, or archaeological culture.
